title: SEC: sieve admin starts unauthenticated when allow_non_loopback=true
description: In smtp/sieve_admin.rs start_sieve_admin_server(), the fail-closed guard is: !is_loopback_addr && !allow_non_loopback && !has_token. When allow_non_loopback=true and no bearer_token is set, the condition is false and the server starts unauthenticated on a network-reachable interface. This allows anyone on the network to read, write, delete, or activate Sieve scripts for any user — full mail filter control without authentication. The test start_non_loopback_allow_override_returns_ok explicitly asserts this succeeds. By contrast, transit/admin.rs and transit/config.rs both require bearer_token even when allow_non_loopback=true. The sieve admin guard should mirror that stronger invariant: non-loopback always requires bearer_token regardless of allow_non_loopback. Trust level: network-adjacent attacker. Worst case: attacker activates a Sieve discard script, silently dropping all incoming mail for a user, or activates a fileinto newsgroup rule exfiltrating mail to a public newsgroup.
